small_guidance:
- Delete the dead `conv_transpose_fused_kernel`, `conv_transpose_kernel_v2`, and `conv_transpose_kernel_v3` stubs entirely — they contain Python syntax (`:=` walrus with `tl.load_to_register`, nested `def`) that breaks module import even though those kernels are never launched. Only keep `conv_transpose_kernel_final`.
- Once the file parses, narrow the autotune grid to 2-3 configs around `BLOCK_OH=4, BLOCK_OW=32, BLOCK_OC=64, BLOCK_IC=16, num_warps=8, num_stages=2` (the M=128, N=64, K=16 GEMM tile that fits this 64×64 IC/OC shape best on RTX 4090).
- Verify the bias sign: `out = tanh((acc + conv_bias) - sub_bias)` ⇒ pass `combined = sub_bias - conv_bias` and compute `acc - combined`, which the code already does — keep this and add a quick scalar test against PyTorch.
large_guidance:
- Keep the parity-split design (per-program constant `kh`, `kw`) since it makes weights compile-time constants and lets `tl.dot` cleanly handle the (M=BLOCK_OH·BLOCK_OW, N=BLOCK_OC, K=BLOCK_IC) GEMM. The structure is sound; the file just needs to be a single clean kernel without the abandoned drafts.
- Consider switching from gather-style (per-output read 4 input taps) to scatter-add: launch one program per `(n, ic_tile, ih_tile, iw_tile)`, compute `input × weight[ic, :, kh, kw]` outer products and `tl.atomic_add` into the 4 output positions. With stride=2 there is no scatter conflict between programs that own disjoint `(ih, iw)` tiles, so atomics are only needed across the IC reduction (or you can accumulate in registers across IC and do a single non-atomic store). This avoids the parity bookkeeping entirely and gives a cleaner `IC×kh×kw → OC` matmul along the contiguous channel axis.
- Fuse the bias subtract and tanh into the epilogue (already done) and use the closed-form `tanh(x) = 1 - 2/(exp(2x)+1)` or `(e2x-1)/(e2x+1)` with a single `tl.exp` instead of two, to halve the special-function cost on the 32·64·512·512 output.
